reader_notes: Read by hand from the note text (dump.ts, bars 0-34), independently: no published analysis consulted. Correspondences between passages were checked note by note with a throwaway comparison script (semitone offsets of aligned notes) and by reading. x = the opening statement, 1:1.5-3:1: a head of five eighths arpeggiating the tonic (F A F C F) and a tail of sixteenths falling stepwise in turns from F5 (2:1 F5, then E D C D C Bb A Bb A G, to F4 at 3:1). y = the sixteenth figure circling a held upper note (A5 C6 Bb5 C6, three times, bar 4) that follows. The bass is silent in bar 1.

notes: Canonic by the protocol's test: the octave canon at one bar runs from 2:1.5 to 8:1.5 and continues at the ninth to 11:2, and the canon returns in bars 12-14 (exchanged), 16-18 and 26-33 (about 25 of 34 bars in canon). Form call (unsure): the main division is the cadence in C at 12; the second half takes the head through C, g and d and then rhymes bars 4-12 a fifth lower (26-34). Because the head itself never returns in the tonic, the form is called bipartite; if the return of the canon from its fourth bar at 26 (in IV, closing in I) counts as a return of the opening, the form is rounded bipartite. The three sections listed treat the IAC in d at 24:1 as a second division; it is weaker than the cadence at 12, so the piece reads as two halves (1-12, 12-34). No y-independent second subject: y is part of the canon. No inversion, augmentation or stretto.
